problem: Customers wanted an easy way to buy and read digital books.
title: Amazon launches the Kindle e-reader at $399
context: Amazon sold books online and had not previously made its own consumer device.
decision_made: Build and sell its own e-reader with built-in wireless book purchasing.
action_taken: Introduced at a press event on 19 November 2007 at $399.
observed_outcome: Amazon said its initial stock sold out in five and a half hours, and the device stayed out of stock for months. The launch inventory was never disclosed.
lessons: Strong initial demand can outstrip supply when volumes are not planned.
limitations: The sell-out figure is from Amazon itself and launch volumes were undisclosed, so it may reflect small inventory. Later sales and profitability were not checked here.

claims.claim_text: Amazon introduced the Kindle on 19 November 2007 at $399.
Amazon said the Kindle sold out of its initial inventory in five and a half hours.
